Changing the props of `TelegramLinkWidget` affects two pages. It's defined in `app/portal/components/TelegramLinkWidget.tsx`.

| Page | Route | Usage |
|---|---|---|
| `app/portal/supplier/page.tsx:715` | `/portal/supplier` | `<TelegramLinkWidget role="supplier" />` |
| `app/portal/reseller/page.tsx:741` | `/portal/reseller` | `<TelegramLinkWidget role="reseller" />` |

Both pages pass only `role`. Other props must be optional, or you'll need to update both call sites.

`test/portal-telegram-widget.test.ts` also uses the component. It builds elements with `{ role: "reseller" }` and `{ role: "supplier" }`, and it checks that both pages embed the widget. Those tests may need updating if you rename or remove `role`.

The widget calls three API routes: `/api/v2/auth/telegram/status`, `/link-token` and `/unlink`. Changing props won't touch them unless the new props change the request payloads.

I used Grep because the atlas tools (`fullstack_impact` and `fullstack_component`) were permission-denied. The search covered direct references by name. It wouldn't catch dynamic imports or re-exports under another name, though I saw none.
